records.supported_name_scope: Rio Itapicuru identifies the connecting trunk toward Conde. Rio Itapicuru-Açu is directly mapped on the upper selected course. Exact feeder, reservoir and name-transition vertices remain unassigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire single selected fragment was inspected: its short north–south western start, eastward Pindobaçu–Ponto Novo passage, Queimadas junction setting, middle eastward bends, Cipó southward turn and lower southeastern coastal approach. The river is Itapicuru in Bahia, not Itapecuru in Maranhão or the Rio Real along the Bahia–Sergipe border.
records.region: Northeastern Bahia, Brazil, from the western Pindobaçu setting through Ponto Novo, Queimadas and Cipó to the Conde coast, south of the Sergipe boundary.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence using readable original INEMA basin-map and IBGE municipal-map pixels. The headward approach, upper named course, reservoirs, middle trunk and terminal coastal setting are accounted for. Exhaustive local feeder naming, surveyed source and mouth positions, and exact name or shoreline transitions are outside this finding; no source acquisition remains pending.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Bahia is an editorial disambiguation, not part of the official river label.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Western headward drainage leading into the mapped Itapicuru-Açu course. The precise initial feeder name and point where each upper label begins are not assigned.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: Pindobaçu, Ponto Novo and the Barragem do Leste setting are impoundment contexts along the selected route, not replacement river names. The modeled line does not establish present water extent, dam-operation status or exact impoundment boundaries.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Aipim, Rio das Pedras, Itapicuru-Mirim and Jacurici remain distinct contributing rivers. The selection does not trace their complete courses. In particular, the northern Itapicuru/Jaguarari approach shown on the regional sheet is not substituted for the actual western Pindobaçu approach.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Itapicuru toward the Conde Atlantic coast. Piranji, Itariri, Rio Real and the ocean remain distinct geographic contexts. No exact estuary or surveyed-mouth boundary is assigned to the selected endpoint.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: One modeled mainstem fragment and its rendered length do not establish a single official source-to-mouth hydronym, natural-river length, perennial flow or modern channel geometry. No historical alias sequence, naming date or Korean form was established.

records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Romaine identifies the connected river system through the northern lake country, the four hydroelectric development sectors and the lower river west of Havre-Saint-Pierre. Initial feeder, lakes, reservoirs and mouth transitions retain separate scopes.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual eastward headward approach and reversal through Lac Long, southward Brûlé passage, southwest-to-east middle bend, sustained southern trunk and final westward turn jointly identify the Romaine corridor. This is distinct from the Magpie and Mingan drainages to the west and Natashquan to the east. Administrative border graphics are geographic context only.
records.region: Québec–Labrador border-region headwaters and Minganie, Côte-Nord, Canada, continuing toward the Gulf of St. Lawrence west of Havre-Saint-Pierre.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence using actual retained PATP map pixels and the independently authored 2019 environmental follow-up map, with later official commissioning prose. Exact feeder naming, waterbody transition vertices, present-day reservoir shorelines and surveyed estuary limits are not assigned. Two unsuccessful optional map acquisitions do not leave the final representative identity unsupported.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Côte-Nord is an editorial disambiguator, not part of the official hydronym.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Selected southern feeder approach into the east end of Lac Long, followed by the westward outlet corridor. Northern mapped headwaters are not substituted for the modeled beginning, and no official name is assigned to its initial feeder or small lake.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Lac Long and Lac Brûlé are separately named waterbodies along the selected upper route. Lac Norman is neighboring branch context. Exact entry and exit vertices are unassigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: There are no separately selected non-mainstem fragments. The initial feeder is nevertheless not automatically named Romaine. Mapped Touladis and de l’Abbé-Huard contributions are separate branches, not aliases or extra selected tributaries.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: The modeled trunk traverses the Romaine 4, 3, 2 and 1 development corridor. The 2019 map supplies reservoir context with an explicitly dated construction state; the 2023 release establishes completion of all four stations. No exact reservoir shoreline, water level, contemporary channel geometry or river-to-reservoir name boundary is established.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: West-turning lower Romaine toward its Gulf of St. Lawrence mouth setting. The full estuary, exact tidal boundary and surveyed mouth are not defined by this line.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Mainstem membership and fragment boundaries do not establish official hydronym boundaries. Rendered length is not an official natural-river length. No formal naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence, historical alias series or Korean form is established. Historical border annotations are not adopted as a territorial-boundary determination.

records.supported_name_scope: Original institutional cartography labels Gran Rio on the southwestern source branch, distinguishes the eastern Pikien Rio branch, marks Lake Brokopondo and labels the downstream Suriname R. Maritime Authority Suriname independently names the lower tidal navigation corridor Suriname River. These scopes support a research candidate, not an administrative naming decision.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The whole modeled route was inspected. Its southwest-to-northeast headward approach, northward upper corridor, northeast turn through the Brokopondo waterbody and northward continuation to Paramaribo jointly distinguish it from the Saramacca drainage to the west and Commewijne drainage to the east. The modeled northern endpoint remains within the lower-river setting, upstream of the Suzannasdaal anchorage identified by the maritime authority.
records.region: Central Suriname, from the interior highlands through the Brokopondo waterbody to the Paramaribo-area lower river.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system correspondence using readable original institutional map pixels and independent official maritime prose and chart-catalog descriptions. The institutional map is not a Suriname government naming or survey decision. Exact headmost feeder, confluence, reservoir shoreline, dam and tidal-boundary vertices remain unassigned. Unavailable optional sources do not prevent this bounded result.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Gran Rio–Brokopondo–Paramaribo is an editorial corridor description, not a single official hydronym.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Southwestern Gran Rio approach and its continuation into the upper Suriname corridor. The map distinguishes Pikien Rio on the eastern source branch. No exact confluence vertex or uniform Gran Rio name is assigned to every headmost modeled segment.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Lake Brokopondo is the source-map label for the intervening waterbody. The selected passage through it is a modeled connecting route, not a claim that a river hydronym applies uniformly across the reservoir. No formal reservoir-name equivalence, dam-name decision or shoreline transition vertex was established.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Tidal lower Suriname in the Paramaribo setting. The maritime publication's bridge and anchorage locations bracket the modeled endpoint in the along-river sequence. The Atlantic mouth, complete estuary and exact tidal limit are not part of the asserted selected-path extent.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: The readable whole-corridor map is credited original cartography published by Nationaal Herbarium Nederland, Universiteit Leiden branch, and hosted by Naturalis. It is an authoritative institutional publication for its own geographic illustration, not a government hydrographic survey or hydronym adjudication. MAS is the official maritime authority; only its acquired prose and public catalog were used, not unacquired commercial chart pixels.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: MAIN_RIV status and the three piece boundaries do not establish uniform names or official hydronym limits. Model length is not an official natural-river length. No naming date, historical alias sequence, Indigenous-name equivalence or Korean form was established.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Chico supports the representative identity of the selected headwater-to-lower-river corridor. The exact initial feeder and the river-to-estuary boundary remain unassigned. The name is not extended to the separate Belgrano, Chalía, Santa Cruz river or whole shared estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete selected single fragment follows the southern Chico Alto approach, eastern upper valley, bends through Gobernador Gregores, long southeastward Chico trunk and northern estuarine approach. This is the Santa Cruz Province river, not other rivers named Chico in Chubut or Tierra del Fuego.
records.region: Central Santa Cruz Province, Argentine Patagonia, from the Chico Alto headwater region through Gobernador Gregores toward the northern Santa Cruz estuarine arm.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence. Exact first named vertex, local source feeder and freshwater–tidal limit remain unassigned; no further acquisition is pending for this assessment.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Santa Cruz, Argentina is editorial disambiguation.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Southern Chico Alto approach; first local feeder and exact start of the hydronym unassigned. The northern Belgrano–Roble/Burmeister route is separate.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Belgrano and Chalía/Sheuen retain distinct scope; they are not aliases or additional selected fragments.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Northern approach to the shared Santa Cruz estuarine setting. Exact river-to-estuary transition and outer mouth unassigned.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: One modeled mainstem fragment does not establish a single hydronym at every vertex, a surveyed river length or present flow conditions.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
